question: Map global airport density on a 10 by 10 degree grid: give me the GeoJSON polygon of every grid cell that contains at least 5 airports together with its airport count, most crowded cells first.
sql:
WITH grid AS (
  SELECT x.i AS gx, y.j AS gy
  FROM generate_series(-18, 17) AS x(i),
       generate_series(-6, 7) AS y(j)
)
SELECT
  g.gx * 10 AS cell_lon_west,
  g.gy * 10 AS cell_lat_south,
  COUNT(*) AS airport_count,
  ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_MakeEnvelope(g.gx * 10.0, g.gy * 10.0, g.gx * 10.0 + 10.0, g.gy * 10.0 + 10.0)) AS cell_geojson
FROM grid g
JOIN airports a
  ON ST_Intersects(
       ST_MakeEnvelope(g.gx * 10.0, g.gy * 10.0, g.gx * 10.0 + 10.0, g.gy * 10.0 + 10.0),
       a.geometry)
GROUP BY g.gx, g.gy
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY airport_count DESC;

question: Compare the four global quadrants — north-west, north-east, south-west and south-east relative to the equator and prime meridian — by number of airports and by average importance rank in each.
sql:
WITH quadrants(name, w, s, e, n) AS (
  VALUES
    ('north-west', -180.0, 0.0, 0.0, 90.0),
    ('north-east', 0.0, 0.0, 180.0, 90.0),
    ('south-west', -180.0, -90.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    ('south-east', 0.0, -90.0, 180.0, 0.0)
)
SELECT
  q.name AS quadrant,
  COUNT(*) AS airport_count,
  ROUND(AVG(a.scalerank), 2) AS avg_importance_rank
FROM quadrants q
JOIN airports a
  ON ST_Intersects(ST_MakeEnvelope(q.w, q.s, q.e, q.n), a.geometry)
GROUP BY q.name
ORDER BY airport_count DESC;

question: Give me the catchment size of each major airport: assign every airport to its nearest major airport and count how many airports each major hub ends up closest to, largest catchment first.
sql:
WITH pairs AS (
  SELECT
    a.name AS airport_name,
    h.name AS hub_name,
    ST_Distance_Spheroid(a.geometry, h.geometry) AS dist_m
  FROM airports a
  JOIN airports h ON h.type = 'major'
),
nearest AS (
  SELECT
    airport_name,
    hub_name,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY airport_name ORDER BY dist_m) AS rn
  FROM pairs
)
SELECT
  hub_name AS major_hub,
  COUNT(*) AS airports_in_catchment
FROM nearest
WHERE rn = 1
GROUP BY hub_name
ORDER BY airports_in_catchment DESC;

question: List the 10 most isolated major airports — for each one, the distance in kilometres to the nearest other airport — starting with the most remote.
sql:
SELECT
  a.name AS airport,
  ROUND(MIN(ST_Distance_Spheroid(a.geometry, b.geometry)) / 1000.0, 1) AS km_to_nearest_airport
FROM airports a
JOIN airports b ON a.name <> b.name
WHERE a.type = 'major'
GROUP BY a.name
ORDER BY km_to_nearest_airport DESC
LIMIT 10;

question: Give me a longitudinal profile of the airport network: for every 30-degree band of longitude from 180°W eastward, the number of airports in the band plus the southernmost and northernmost airport latitudes found inside it.
sql:
WITH strips AS (
  SELECT i FROM generate_series(-6, 5) AS g(i)
)
SELECT
  s.i * 30 AS band_lon_west,
  (s.i + 1) * 30 AS band_lon_east,
  COUNT(*) AS airport_count,
  ROUND(MIN(ST_Y(a.geometry)), 2) AS southernmost_lat,
  ROUND(MAX(ST_Y(a.geometry)), 2) AS northernmost_lat
FROM strips s
JOIN airports a
  ON ST_Intersects(ST_MakeEnvelope(s.i * 30.0, -90.0, (s.i + 1) * 30.0, 90.0), a.geometry)
GROUP BY s.i
ORDER BY s.i;

question: From the mid-Pacific point at 21.3°N, 157.9°W, give me one row per radius showing how many airports lie within 500 km, 1,000 km, 2,000 km and 4,000 km.
sql:
WITH rings(radius_km) AS (
  VALUES (500), (1000), (2000), (4000)
)
SELECT
  r.radius_km AS within_km,
  COUNT(*) AS airports_within
FROM rings r
JOIN airports a
  ON ST_DWithin_Spheroid(a.geometry, ST_Point(-157.9, 21.3), r.radius_km * 1000.0)
GROUP BY r.radius_km
ORDER BY r.radius_km;
